configuration.maintenance_intent: No free-space or size pressure on this tiny root; pre-workload pressure-only automatic GC should skip. First post-workload automatic GC is due because no previous success exists; require the existing success metadata to establish actual automatic maintenance, not merely explicit gc availability. Later rounds may be throttled by interval_hours=1.
configuration.write_timing: Only after later allocated config init-root creates the product-owned root/config, replace the task-owned generated config with this documented schema then config check; no host config changes. max_bytes, cargo.real_path and sccache.cache_size are omitted Option fields, not invented null TOML values.

environment.reason: Unmanaged inherited native cache overrides are intentionally respected by the product and would invalidate this routed-lease case. Do not read user configuration to find them; create the explicit case environment. No policy/credential values are copied.

after_each_outer_reaped.require: applied=true, complete=true, failures=[], no active task lease records, stable root-lock inode, public output payload retained by the normal120-day policy. This demonstrates normal exclusive maintenance became available.

gc_observations.automatic_followthrough: Require the existing control/last-automatic-gc.json first success after success-outer: complete=true/last_success_unix present/pressure=false. Derive exact platform control location from product observation/source layout. Record marker absence before first outer and success afterward; merely returning outer exit0 is insufficient because automatic-GC errors are best effort.

during_each_gate.require: Prompt coordinated busy failure before mutation, not command timeout. Product currently maps busy errors to12; do not substitute standard generic3.
during_each_gate.stdout: No successful JSON document required for the error path; current main_entry reports busy on stderr.

during_each_gate.require: applied=false; complete=true on this small clean root; failures=[]; abstentions contain active-resource reason for the routed temp sentinel. Preserve exact sentinel hash/payload and stable control/root.lock device+inode. Preview may report hypothetical actions elsewhere; it must not apply them.

optional_decisive_preview_eligibility.use: Source-grounded stronger active-resource preview only, if needed to make the sentinel an eligible candidate absent its lease. It is never used for applied maintenance and never changes config. Existing active-resource abstention is checked before selection; do not infer broader cleanup authority.

gc_observations.timing: Proposed per busy/preview observation budget10s, both real native compiler/linker invocations max60s each, all still bounded by the one600s execution clock. A miss is failure/stop, never proof of safety.

activated=false on repeat; installed cc and ccache intercepts resolve to this candidate with no recursion.
Fresh unmarked empty ROOT only; no --force-config. This command is dispatched before effective Config::load, so an absent explicit CONFIG is supported here.
valid=true after writing only the task TOML template.

enabled/root_valid true, configured_root ROOT, intercept directory INTERCEPTS, worktree equals outside-checkout WORK, ccache/temp route actually active. Do not require unrelated disabled adapters/tools to be healthy.
Returned path TMP_RESOURCE lies within this task-owned root; select it from JSON rather than guessing platform/runtime layout.
Future task-only script implements the foreground gate protocol below. DevCache itself invokes no interpreter: Python is the explicitly user-owned child workload only.
One intentional invalid-C compiler failure, not a retry of success. The script and outer DevCache return exactly that native compiler exit status; no fake tool replacement.
No task active lease remains after direct children are reaped; runtime-root identity unchanged; resource completion metadata reflects settled foreground work.

optional_existing_updateall_owner_lane.clock: If included, these native operations consume this same separately allocated600s. If not ready or insufficient remaining time, leave UNRUN; no automatic second clock.

optional_existing_updateall_owner_lane.host_operands: HOST_* are deliberately unbound until normal fresh owner/receipt discovery. Never reuse case HOME/env to mutate the host lane or use task self-install over its managed alias.
optional_existing_updateall_owner_lane.require: Fresh selected updater identity and normal receipt/journal admission. After update require installed013 with retained012; rollback must restore the receipt-owned012, preserve accepted013 authority and retain013; exact same signed013 offline reapply restores013/previous012. Verify alias/binary hashes/build-info and owned intercept targets after each. No forced receipt rewrite, accepted-generation reset, old-version manifest intake, cleanup of rollback bytes, or network.

outer_workload_protocol.implementation_state: UNPREPARED; these are exact fixed future child argv and protocol requirements, not an executable runner or proof of runtime behavior.
outer_workload_protocol.proof_limits: Tiny cc may finish before a concurrent observation. Before/after gated observations prove outer exclusion spanning the nested launch; nested activity and real route are corroborated by product resource/activity metadata and resulting real executable. This is not a claim that a tiny compiler was observed active at a particular sampling instant.
schedule: Start one foreground outer through exec temp. Future outer script creates only one public sentinel at inherited TMPDIR/acceptance-sentinel and announces READY_BEFORE_NESTED; then blocks on a pipe gate owned by the orchestrator. This proves the outer lease is active before nested setup.
At READY_BEFORE_NESTED, run the concurrent GC pair below and hash sentinel plus relevant task payload/lock identities before and after each command.

Release the gate. Success invokes the installed cc intercept for real compile and separate real link, drains/reaps each, runs the new program, requires exactly dev-cache-013-native-ok\n and exit0. Failure invokes the real invalid-C compilation once, records the real nonzero code/diagnostics, drains/reaps it, and later exits with that same code.

After nested command settlement, outer announces READY_AFTER_NESTED and remains foreground/active behind the second pipe gate. Run the GC pair again before permitting outer exit. No sleeps are evidence of active lifetime.

Release second gate, outer emits fixed success/failure completion metadata and returns preserved native status; reap outer and its owned child chain. Check automatic maintenance metadata after success, then explicit post-settlement GC.

For failure, compare exact public compiler stdout/stderr and status to one direct REAL_CC baseline with same source/output operands and LC_ALL=C. Expected compiler error is successful observation only if identities/status/output match; any unexpected mismatch stops. Do not classify arbitrary nonzero as the intended failure.
outer_workload_protocol.stdio: Task protocol/status and pure public compiler diagnostics may be bounded and retained. Never pipe/capture native auth streams. Build bounded output/drain and owned-child settlement into the later small task script before execution. No background children or detached jobs.

purpose: Native installed acceptance of full active-workload shared root lease across nested real compiler/linker setup; not a test suite or performance campaign.

remaining_before_execution: Parent allocate distinct 600+60 native acceptance scope and reconcile shared compiler owner.
Require actual exact-source signed candidate A/B qualification and release verification; PREPARATION.json candidate path is only a future selector.
Bind existing real native cc/ccache/linker and task Python identities, ensure they are native upstream rather than existing intercepts, and verify no ambient cache override causes abstention.
Prepare only this small task-local foreground orchestrator/outer script, gate protocol and public C inputs; none is written by this plan.
Require a fresh private canonical outside-checkout case root with current UID, no existing case results, no foreign cache/installation state.

settlement_and_evidence.deadline: 600 is the requested execution bound,60 settlement allowance; kernel-blocked I/O and uncertain external ownership can exceed this. Then keep logical ownership and explicitly report unsettled/unknown; never claim a hard kernel bound or free-lock release.
settlement_and_evidence.failure: Stop launching subsequent steps at first unexpected outcome or deadline. Preserve partial files/results and any product-owned journals. Close task-owned gates and settle only known owned foreground clients/children under existing controller rules; do not kill an uncertain install/auth owner. No broad PGID/cgroup/foreign process signals or lock-file deletion.
keep: Exact source/build identity and authenticated input hashes
Native argv/executable identities/custody selected for this public case
Per-step elapsed/status and bounded public diagnostics
Gates, sentinel/payload hashes, activity/resource evidence, root lock device+inode before/after
GC structured reports and fixed busy outcome
Automatic maintenance success record and final installed/rollback receipt state if selected
settlement_and_evidence.standalone_claim: Product binaries and native compiler prerequisites operate outside a checkout with no private consumer/code/config, interpreter hook or sibling product requirement. The optional Python task orchestrator and optional UpdateAll management are acceptance tools, not mandatory DevCache runtime dependencies.
